experiment: Exp B data ladder — data axis for the new architectures (Pythia-160M, SmolLM2-135M) across OWT/C4/RefinedWeb/DCLM, small size only
metric: data-CEG vs the shared external bar = the size-matched GPT-2-trained-on-OWT threshold (b160=1.251829 for Pythia-160M, b135=1.272076 for SmolLM2-135M). data-CEG = GPU-hours for that GPT-2-OWT baseline to reach the bar / GPU-hours for the architecture-on-corpus to reach the SAME bar (log-hours interpolation, study method). A run that never reaches the bar is CENSORED. Using one fixed external bar (not each arch's own OWT quality) is deliberate: it makes 'crosses the bar' mean 'beats a matched GPT-2', which is the headline.
size_note: Small size only (~135-160M): overlays Exp A's 124M ladder; data multiplier is scale-stable; small avoids SmolLM2's size-worsening OWT divergence. All 6 arms = exact B1 8-GPU config (global batch 524288, 8.87B tokens, union eval).
findings: Better data flips both new architectures from LOSING to a matched GPT-2 (censored on OWT/C4) to BEATING it (crosses on RefinedWeb/DCLM), with a 4.6-6.4x data-CEG.

Corpus progress is not monotonic with release date. Under the Exp B threshold, neither OWT nor C4 produces a measurable CEG: neither reaches the reference threshold. Their terminal BPBs are similar, with C4 marginally lower in both tested architectures, while RefinedWeb and DCLM show substantially stronger improvements. This reproduces Exp A's non-monotonic-in-release-year data-quality finding across two further independent architectures (GPT-NeoX and Llama lineages).
The data lever (crosses the GPT-2 bar) is far larger than the architecture lever (B1: no new arch beats GPT-2 on OWT at all).
